title: Introduce SpectraAttn microkernel and Rope Harmonizer for low-latency KV warmup
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces SpectraAttn microkernel (FP16/INT8 fastpath) and Rope Harmonizer to reduce KV cache warmup and p99 latency; opt-in via runtime flags; rollout behind canary and feature toggle.
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end token latency and warmup overhead for long-context streaming workloads while preserving generation quality. This PR adds a new microkernel (SpectraAttn) optimized for mid-sized sequence windows and a complementary Rope Harmonizer that fuses rotary/rope handling into the attention hotpath and coordinates KV warmup lanes for continuous batching. Design highlights: 1) SpectraAttn microkernel implements a vectorized qk/v reduction that reorders memory layouts for better L2 locality and uses fused qk softmax + v-prod to reduce memory traffic; it exposes two execution modes: fp16-accum (default) and int8-quantized fastpath (optional). 2) Rope Harmonizer merges rotary embedding application with recurrence-aware prefix matching to avoid duplicate rotational transforms in cached KV lookups. 3) Continuous windowed-batching scheduler: requests are grouped into sliding windows and assigned warmup lanes so KV caches pre-populate the most-likely prefixes asynchronously, reducing p99 for first-response in streaming scenarios. 4) Compatibility layer: new kernel registers as an alternative implementation in kernel registry and falls back to existing attn path if shapes/precision not supported. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on p4d: SpectraAttn fp16 yields 12%-18% lower p50 token latency and 20%-28% lower p99 across 1k-8k sequences compared to current tuned kernel; int8 fastpath shown 1.6x throughput in high-concurrency synthetic tests with negligible quality regression on eval set (perplexity delta <0.6%). End-to-end service tests with continuous batching show median first-token reduction of 40-60ms on typical chat traces and p99 reduction ~25% for streamed responses. Backwards compatibility & rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag --use-spectra-attn and orchestrated canary (10%->50%->100%) with automatic rollback on new SLO regressions. Tests & CI: added unit tests for fused rotary correctness, kernel invariants, and added e2e benchmarks to perf-lab harness. Also extended trace spans for KV warmup lanes for observability. Checklist: [x] kernel implementation and unit tests [x] integration with kernel registry [x] scheduler changes and e2e bench harness updates [x] docs update (runtime flag + tuning guide) [x] canary rollout plan. Related: ENG-1742 (attn latency project), SUP-4128 (customer reported p99 spikes during streaming).

extra_context: This PR aims to be synergistic with previous scheduling work (windowed batcher series) but focuses on a hotpath kernel rewrite and a small harmonizer that avoids redundant rotary application during cache lookups. The changes are self-contained; fallback path preserved.
notes_on_testing: Unit tests cover fused rotary algebra, invariants for QKV transposes, and quantization recovery; perf-lab ran 12-hour soak for continuous batching traces. DDP cross-device tests added to prevent subtle broadcast issues.
